question: Which Linux companion app path should OpenClaw pursue now that Windows Hub is documented and shipped: the GTK/C PR, the Rust/GTK4 alternative, or a narrower/deferred Linux milestone plan?
rationale: The issue is no longer a simple missing-platform bug; the remaining work requires choosing architecture, packaging, ownership, and security posture across large native app surfaces.

options.title: Choose one Linux app track
options.body: Pick a preferred Linux app implementation, close or park the alternative, and require focused security, packaging, and real-behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Split into milestone issues
options.body: Keep this umbrella but open narrower Linux milestones for packaging, gateway pairing, tray/status, chat, and node capability parity before accepting a large app PR.

options.title: Defer Linux app work
options.body: Leave Linux on the supported Gateway/CLI path for now and revisit the native companion app after security/core priorities settle.

recommendation.title: Choose one Linux app track
recommendation.body: Pick a preferred Linux app implementation, close or park the alternative, and require focused security, packaging, and real-behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the request and product-direction comments and is the strongest routing signal for platform app direction in the available history.
